scenes.headline: RBAC
scenes.subtitle: Role-based access control in Unity Catalog
scenes.narration: Role-based access control governs who can see and act on data objects across your Databricks workspaces.

scenes.headline: How RBAC is structured
items: Privileges granted to groups, not individuals
Objects organized as catalog, schema, and table
scenes.narration: Best practice assigns privileges to groups so access scales cleanly. Data is organized in a three-level namespace of catalog, schema, and table. Grants flow downward, so a catalog grant covers its schemas and tables.

scenes.headline: Granting privileges
scenes.narration: We grant the finance group traversal and read access down to the sales schema. A single SELECT grant on the schema covers all its tables. We then revoke access to one sensitive table to enforce least privilege.

scenes.headline: Group-based vs user-based grants
scenes.narration: Granting to groups keeps access consistent and easy to audit. Managing per-user grants quickly becomes unmanageable and inconsistent. Tying groups to your identity provider centralizes governance.

scenes.headline: Principles to follow
scenes.narration: Grant only the access each role genuinely needs. Managing permissions in Unity Catalog gives one governed model across workspaces. Periodic reviews catch drift and stale access before it becomes risk.

scenes.text: Grant to groups, follow least privilege, and let inheritance do the rest.
scenes.narration: Well-designed RBAC means access is obvious, auditable, and easy to reason about.
